title: Develop a "Data Privacy & Security" One-Pager for University IT
description: Universities are highly sensitive about data. Zedu emphasizes secure data infrastructure and role-based permissions. Draft a one-page summary of Zedu's privacy features, tailored for a university IT director's approval process.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Privacy-First SEO Landing Pages for University IT
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Build a set of highly specific landing pages targeting university procurement and IT directors (e.g., "HIPAA-compliant learning workspaces for universities"). These pages should focus on the technical evidence of Zedu s security and privacy, converting high-value institutional leads who prioritize data residency and student privacy over feature sets.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Source-map every claim in the one-pager to a public page, flagging unsupported ones as gaps
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Before publishing, audit the one-pager sentence by sentence: each security or privacy claim gets a citation to an existing public Zedu page (privacy policy, security page, terms) with an access date, or it is flagged as an unsupported gap the team must either source or cut. Deliverable: the annotated draft plus the gap list. This prevents the one-pager from stating anything a university IT reviewer could disprove in five minutes.

upvotes.reason: "Source-map every claim in the one-pager to a public page, flagging unsupported ones as gaps" gives the team evidence it can act on, with every claim carrying its source, so the result holds up when someone checks it. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Turn university IT review questions into a sourced one-page evidence sheet
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Start from the questions a university IT reviewer is likely to ask, then map each answer to evidence Zedu can actually show: a policy clause, verified product behaviour, code reference or named team confirmation. Keep each row to the question, the confirmed answer, its source and the person who can confirm it. Mark anything unverified as a question for the team instead of making a broad security promise. Summarise the confirmed points on one page and link to the full policy or trust material for detail. This adapts verified evidence for an IT review, rather than repeating the broader public trust page.
